transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-03-13 16:00 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Rajiv Kapoor (Redwood SE), Sam Patel (Redwood CSM), Elena Morales (Harbor - Procurement), Dr. Marcus Li (Harbor - CTO), Tara Nguyen (Harbor - Legal), Omar Ruiz (Harbor - Cloud)
Summary (auto): Roundtable to align commercial path, discuss redlines to the MSA/DPA, SLA expectations for Dedicated vs Hosted, KMS/HSM requirements, and pricing approval process. Agreed next steps on redlines, pricing approver list, and technical benchmark timeline.

00:00:03 - Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for doing this roundtable, appreciate you fitting it in. we thought this format could help unblock both legal and procurement threads at once.
00:00:12 - Elena Morales: yeah thanks Maya, a lot of folks on our side wanted a single sync. we have parallel review happening so want to make sure the commercial path and the legal redlines don't diverge.
00:00:25 - Rajiv Kapoor: quick intro from our side, i'm rajiv, i'll be the SE for the benchmark work and the technical details — happy to dive deep later.
00:00:38 - Dr. Marcus Li: morning all. from a tech POV the big items are private deployment latency SLA, encryption at rest with customer-managed keys, and onboarding time.
00:00:50 - Tara Nguyen: and i'm tara, i'll be handling the legal review for Harbor. our main asks: DPA language on data retention, breach notification timelines, indemnity carve-outs and audit access.
00:01:05 - Maya Chen: great, let's structure — quick commercial readout, then legal redlines, then tech SLOs, finally an ops/pricing approver checklist.
00:01:18 - Elena Morales: perfect. on pricing, our procurement committee needs a clear escalation path: what happens when we exceed committed capacity, and what approval steps are required for overage billing.
00:01:33 - Maya Chen: understood. Redwood supports both usage-based and committed reserved lanes. for Dedicated we typically use a monthly commit contract with defined burst buckets. pricing overage flows can be routed to finance or to AE for immediate alerts — we'll put that in the commercial matrix.
00:01:52 - Elena Morales: can you send the matrix? also, we need to know if price escalators or CPI adjustments are built into the MSA.
00:01:59 - Maya Chen: yes, we'll send the matrix. we generally don't have automatic CPI clauses at the short term but there are enterprise-tier negotiation points. we'll flag any escalator language in the redline.
00:02:10 - Tara Nguyen: moving to the MSA/DPA redlines — our counsel has three high-priority items: 1) indemnity limitation clarity, 2) data subject request handling timeline and 3) audit rights.
00:02:22 - Maya Chen: ok, can you share the specific language you want changed or is the legal team looking for alternative wording?
00:02:28 - Tara Nguyen: we've uploaded a marked DPA; the main ask is a 30-day notice for export of customer data for backups, and a 72-hour notification window for suspected breaches that impact PHI.
00:02:40 - Rajiv Kapoor: note — in a hosted model our incident detection systems will surface anomalies earlier but cross-region failover can make 72 hours tight to confirm scope. in Dedicated/private we can map notification to our on-prem monitoring hooks.
00:02:55 - Dr. Marcus Li: just to be clear, Harbor handles PHI so the 72-hour requirement is a regulatory non-negotiable for our board.
00:03:04 - Omar Ruiz: also need to confirm data residency guarantees for EU vs US workloads; some of our clinics are in EU, so we need region pinning or guaranteed processing in eu-west-1.
00:03:17 - Maya Chen: that's doable — Redwood Private can be deployed into EU regions and we support routing policies. we'll capture region pinning as a contractual SLI.
00:03:27 - Elena Morales: on KMS — our security requires customer-managed keys with HSM-backed storage; we can't accept provider-managed keys for certain datasets.
00:03:38 - Rajiv Kapoor: we support KMS integrations and can do bring-your-own-key via KMS/HSM; we need to confirm whether Harbor requires HSM-only key material and an HSM attestation.
00:03:49 - Tara Nguyen: yes, HSM-only for certain PHI tiers. we also want to confirm whether Redwood has an SOC 2 report and if a Type II is available.
00:03:59 - Maya Chen: yes we have SOC 2 Type II and can share the report under an NDA. we'll also include our security pack link in the follow-up.
00:04:08 - Elena Morales: great. can you also clarify audit logs retention? our auditors want 2 years of immutable logs.
00:04:16 - Rajiv Kapoor: by default we keep logs 1 year, but enterprise plans can extend retention or stream to customer S3 for immutability. we'll note the streaming option as contractual addendum.
00:04:28 - Elena Morales: ok that helps.
00:04:34 - Maya Chen: let's switch to SLA expectations. Marcus, what would be acceptable for you in terms of p50/p95 latency and uptime SLA?
00:04:43 - Dr. Marcus Li: for patient-facing queries p95 < 250ms is ideal, p50 < 120ms. uptime target 99.95 for core inference endpoints. if that's not feasible we'll consider a hybrid where critical flows hit a dedicated lane.
00:05:00 - Rajiv Kapoor: technical note: p95 250ms for medium-size models in Dedicated is plausible with right batching configs and prefix caching; hosted may meet lower throughput but can vary with multi-tenant spikes. we can propose canary routing to Dedicated for critical flows.
00:05:18 - Omar Ruiz: about rollout — how long does a private deployment take from signed MSA to production? we need an estimate to include in project planning.
00:05:27 - Maya Chen: canonical timeline: for Redwood Private in a customer-managed VPC it's about 6-8 weeks once infra is provisioned; for on-prem it depends on hardware procurement but we can do a pilot in 2-3 weeks using a dedicated cloud sandbox.
00:05:41 - Elena Morales: that's reasonable. procurement will want a fixed window for onboarding milestones in the MSA.
00:05:48 - Tara Nguyen: back to the DPA — do you offer subprocessor lists and 30-day prior notice before adding new subprocessors?
00:05:55 - Maya Chen: yes we maintain a subprocessors list and can agree to 30-day notice for new ones, standard practice.
00:06:04 - Dr. Marcus Li: curious about data deletion proof — can Redwood provide a certificate of deletion or attestation after deletion?
00:06:12 - Rajiv Kapoor: we can provide deletion receipts and logs for customer datasets; for cached KV the retention window is configurable, and we can publish deletion proofs as part of the offboarding flow.
00:06:25 - Elena Morales: procurement question — we need a pricing approver workflow. who signs off on overages, and can we set automated budget alerts before hitting thresholds?
00:06:34 - Maya Chen: yes, we can set automated alerts and webhook notifications, and we can gate overage charges to require a named approver in the contract. we'll include a process map showing who to notify (finance, procurement, AE).
00:06:48 - Tara Nguyen: legal redline item: limitation of liability — we need carve-outs for willful misconduct and willful breach relating to PHI.
00:06:58 - Maya Chen: we usually accept carve-outs for gross negligence and willful misconduct; we can review exact wording in the redline.
00:07:06 - Rajiv Kapoor: technical aside — for PHI we recommend Dedicated + KMS with HSM and private networking to minimize blast radius.
00:07:14 - Dr. Marcus Li: agreed. is there a cost delta estimate for HSM-only keys vs standard keys?
00:07:21 - Maya Chen: HSM keying typically adds an integration premium and operational fee; i'll have pricing on that in the commercial sheet.
00:07:29 - Elena Morales: about insurance — we need confirmation of cyber insurance limits; our threshold is 10M.
00:07:36 - Maya Chen: Redwood carries cyber insurance with limits that meet industry norms; i'll include a certificate of insurance in the follow-up.
00:07:44 - Tara Nguyen: question: do you allow penetration tests by customers or third-party auditors?
00:07:50 - Rajiv Kapoor: yes, under controlled conditions and with coordination; we have an established penetration test intake process and can accommodate scheduled tests in a dedicated environment.
00:07:59 - Omar Ruiz: network egress — can we cap egress or have predictable egress charges for EU data?
00:08:07 - Maya Chen: egress billing can be itemized and we can agree to capped egress tiers in the SOW for Dedicated/Private.
00:08:15 - Elena Morales: let's talk timeline for the redline: can you get a consolidated Redwood redline by mid-week?
00:08:20 - Maya Chen: yes, we'll consolidate and highlight the non-negotiables. target 2025-03-18.
00:08:26 - Tara Nguyen: procurement will then run a pricing approval, which takes about 5 business days once we have the commercial sheet.
00:08:33 - Maya Chen: understood — we'll aim to get commercial sheet same day as redline.
00:08:39 - Rajiv Kapoor: for the technical benchmark — propose a 4-stage plan: 1) baseline hosted test with sample prompts, 2) Dedicated pilot with model quantization, 3) KV/prefix cache sim to estimate cost per 1M tokens, 4) failure/fallback test across regions. should take 1-2 weeks to run depending on data prep.
00:08:57 - Dr. Marcus Li: that sounds good. also want us to simulate peak clinic hours to observe tail latency.
00:09:05 - Rajiv Kapoor: noted, we'll include peak-hour load profile.
00:09:11 - Elena Morales: are there any product-specific contractual terms we should watch for? e.g., retention of model weights, co-territory clauses?
00:09:19 - Maya Chen: model weights are not customer data; however we can agree to usage restrictions if you provide sensitive training data. co-territory clauses we can review but standard MSA keeps rights limited.
00:09:29 - Tara Nguyen: legal redline detail request — where is the data processing addendum hosted?
00:09:34 - Maya Chen: link included in the calendar — we'll attach the latest DPA and indicate redline points. shared resource: https://redwood.example.com/security/redwood-dpa-v3.pdf (will send under NDA).
00:09:47 - Elena Morales: good. competitor question — our security team asked whether you rely on any third-party inference accelerators from Anthropic or BigCloud — any exclusivity or subprocessor concerns?
00:09:59 - Maya Chen: we don't have exclusivity with other model vendors; we have a curated catalog. if a model execution path uses a third-party accelerator that is a subprocess we disclose that on the subprocessor list.
00:10:12 - Omar Ruiz: procurement note: contract alignment with our internal SSO provider — we use Okta and require SAML SSO plus SCIM provisioning.
00:10:21 - Rajiv Kapoor: Redwood supports SAML/SSO and SCIM provisioning for user accounts. we'll include Okta SCIM setup notes.
00:10:30 - Tara Nguyen: one more legal Q — can you share retention of audit logs and whether logs are tamper-evident?
00:10:37 - Rajiv Kapoor: logs can be streamed to customer-owned storage to provide immutability; we can offer append-only and WORM policies when pushing to S3 with object lock.
00:10:48 - Elena Morales: ok.
00:10:50 - Maya Chen: quick recap: Redwood to send consolidated MSA/DPA redline and commercial matrix by 2025-03-18, include SOC 2 Type II, COI, subprocessor list, and HSM integration notes. Harbor to provide pricing approver list by 2025-03-17 and confirm HSM requirement and contact. Redwood to propose technical benchmark plan by 2025-03-21 and schedule pilot week of 2025-03-24.
00:11:18 - Tara Nguyen: correct. we'll internally queue legal review once we receive the redline.
00:11:24 - Dr. Marcus Li: and we'll prepare a list of 3 priority endpoints for low-latency routing during the pilot.
00:11:31 - Rajiv Kapoor: i'll include a spreadsheet template for workload profiles and token estimates.
00:11:37 - Elena Morales: thanks all, this was really useful to align.
00:11:41 - Maya Chen: thanks everyone. we'll follow up in the calendar with the redline and prep items.

(Transcript continues with shorter Q&A and confirmations; timestamps approximate, occasional transcription errors present.)

22:30:12 - Speaker 4: (inaudible) redwood - sometimes shows as red wood console in notes (sic), but link is in the deck.
23:01:05 - Maya Chen: action items captured, I'll send the deck and redline.
